decisive_items: alveoli filled with inflammatory debris consisting of granulation tissue, interstitial inflammation, and areas of intra-alveolar fibrin deposition
Repeat BAL was negative for AFB, fungus, and Pneumocystis jirovecii
new patchy peribronchovascular consolidations in the right upper lobe, left upper lobe, and left lower-lobe apical segment
response.rationale: The transbronchial biopsy is diagnostic of organizing pneumonia with intra-alveolar fibrin deposition, and repeat BAL excludes active PCP, fungal, and mycobacterial infection. The radiographic pattern of peribronchovascular consolidations after resolution of ground-glass opacities also fits organizing pneumonia.

rejected.why: Idiopathic pneumonia syndrome is a post-hematopoietic stem cell transplant syndrome, not supported by renal transplant or this biopsy pattern.
No fungal hyphae were seen on BAL or biopsy, and repeat BAL was negative for fungus.
Initial PCP was treated and resolved; repeat BAL was negative for PCP and biopsy shows organizing pneumonia, not Pneumocystis.
No evidence specifically implicates mycophenolate; the biopsy shows organizing pneumonia without drug-toxicity features.
Interstitial lung disease is too broad; the biopsy provides a specific organizing pneumonia pattern.
CMV was excluded by negative inclusion bodies and no viral cytopathic effect on biopsy.
No evidence specifically implicates tacrolimus; the biopsy and negative microbiology favor organizing pneumonia rather than drug-induced pneumonitis.
